reason: Book print-on-demand was already mainstream before the band: Bowker counted non-traditional, mostly POD titles above traditional titles from 2008, and nearly 8 times as many in 2010, 7 years before the 2015 band end. On-demand manufacturing of objects (Shapeways-style 3D printing services) stayed niche through 2015. Under the MATERIALS reading, real but niche adoption by 2015 gives partial; the book reading gives an early forecast of 5+ years, also no better than partial.

Industrial/consumer test. HP planned memristor memory with Hynix for 2013 but dropped it from The Machine in 2015 and used DRAM instead. Resistive RAM exists only in niche embedded memory. Memristors were not mainstream by 2020 (band end + 5) or today, so this is a miss.

Test: industrial standard practice. Cermet cutting tools were introduced in the 1950s and Sumitomo launched TiC-based cermet inserts in 1960; cermets were an established tooling class decades before the 2011-2015 band. The early rule puts mainstream arrival more than 5 years before the placed year in miss: the forecast was late by about 50 years. It is not unfalsifiable because the label names a clear material class.

Energy test. Ultracapacitors had real commercial uses by 2015 (hybrid buses, rail, wind-turbine pitch control, some automotive start-stop), but the market was small: leader Maxwell's ultracapacitor revenue fell to $114.5 million in 2015. They took no material share of energy storage, which lithium-ion batteries dominated. Real niche adoption at the band end gives partial; not a miss because commercial deployment existed.

Test: abstract practice routinely occurring. Gamification peaked as a trend in 2011-2013 and spread in apps (Foursquare, Duolingo streaks, social TV check-ins), but in media proper it stayed a set of experiments; Gartner predicted in 2012 that 80% of gamified applications would fail by 2014, and many media badge programmes closed. Real but niche adoption within the band, so partial. Not a hit because gamified news or TV consumption never became normal practice.

By 2015, 52% of US households had Netflix, Amazon Prime or Hulu, and digital overtook physical in global recorded music revenue with streaming growing 45%. That meets the consumer test (well over 10% of households) inside the 2011-2015 band. 'All' media was not fully on demand (live TV persisted), but the dominant formats were.

Consumer test. Pew measured US adult e-reader ownership at 24% in September 2013 and 32% in January 2014, and e-ink shelf labels spread in retail. Mainstream by 2013-2014 is within 2 years of 2015, so this is a hit. It is not early by more than 2 years, because ownership was still below about 12% in 2011.

Test: infrastructure used by a large share of users. Bluetooth PAN was already mainstream before the band: the one-billionth Bluetooth device shipped in November 2006 at 12 million per week. PAN was mainstream during 2011-2015, but it arrived about 4-5 years before the band opened, so the forecast was late; partial under the early rule. If the poster meant BLE wearable networks specifically, 2013-2015 wearables would make it a hit.

Consumer test. Social networking use among US adults rose to 65% by 2015, and Facebook's social graph powered login and sharing across the web through Facebook Connect and Open Graph. The social graph was mainstream inside the 2011 to 2015 band. Hit by the band rule.

Test: infrastructure widely deployed. Schema.org launched in 2011; by 2015, 31.3% of pages in a 10-billion-page sample carried schema.org markup, and Google, Bing and Yahoo consumed it for rich results and knowledge graphs. Mainstream by the band end 2015, so hit. The strict W3C vision (RDF/OWL reasoning by software agents across the web) stayed niche; under that reading the verdict is partial.

Schema.org launched in 2011, Google's Knowledge Graph in 2012 and Wikidata in 2012. By 2015, 31.3% of sampled web pages carried schema.org markup, up from 22% a year earlier, and search engines used it routinely. That meets the infrastructure test (widely deployed and used) inside the 2011-2015 band, though as pragmatic structured data rather than the full Semantic Web vision.

Medical test. The FDA list held about 1,250 AI-enabled devices by end-2025, over three quarters in radiology. An ESR survey found 48% of European radiologists using AI clinically in 2024, up from 20% in 2018. Approved, widely used diagnostic AI inside the 2015-2025 band makes this a hit. Reimbursement stays limited and adoption outside radiology is thin, which is the main argument for partial.

Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2030. Test: industrial standard practice (flight use). VASIMR has never flown. Its best result is an 88-hour, 80 kW ground endurance test in July 2021 under NASA NextSTEP, aiming at TRL 5. Nothing shows a flight unit being built, so mainstream use by 2030 is very unlikely. Miss, provisional until the window closes in 2030.

Infrastructure test. The flagship superconducting intertie, Tres Amigas, lost its Eastern link in 2015 and went silent after 2017. Superconducting cables that do run in grids (LIPA 2008, AmpaCity Essen, Shanghai 2021, Munich SuperLink in testing in 2024 to 2025) are short distribution or urban links, not interties. No superconducting intertie is in commercial service by 2025. Miss, and the intertie form was abandoned.

Test: energy, material share of the market. LFP cathodes, which depend on nanoscale carbon-coated particles to overcome low conductivity, reached almost half of the global EV battery market by 2024 per the IEA. Mainstream inside the 2015-2025 band. Hit. Caveat: commercial LFP uses sub-micron primary particles and nanocoatings rather than exotic nanostructures such as nanowires, which stayed in the lab.

In 2016 solar PV added over 74 GW and grew faster than any other fuel, with auction prices near 3 US cents/kWh. IRENA found utility PV costs fell 85% from 2010 to 2020 and most new renewables undercut the cheapest new fossil option by 2020. PV became a material share of new capacity at grid parity inside the 2015-2025 band (energy test).

Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2030. Energy test. Global CSP capacity reached only about 6.9 GW by 2024, against about 1,865 GW of solar PV; CSP is a negligible share of new capacity. PV displaced it. Solar water heating is a separate case: it was already mainstream in China before 2011 and its market has shrunk since 2013, so that reading is also a miss (early). Either reading gives miss. Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2030.

Test: consumer product at 10%+ of people. Pew found 74% of US smartphone owners used location-based services in early 2012, when about 46% of adults owned smartphones, so roughly a third of adults already used location-aware content in 2012. It was mainstream through the band, but it arrived about 3 years before the 2015-2025 band opened; the forecast was late, which the early rule grades partial. A hit would need mainstream arrival within the band.

Consumer test. By 2025 real niche forms existed: immersive projection venues such as Sphere Las Vegas (opened 2023), immersive art exhibitions, and holographic displays such as Looking Glass monitors. The holographic display market was only about $4.3 billion in 2025 and served B2B, retail and entertainment niches. It never became a common interface in homes or offices within the 2015 to 2025 band. Partial for real niche adoption; the label is loose, which is a second reason not to go further.

Test: consumer and industrial practice widely deployed. By the early 2020s about 47% of items received by apparel and general-merchandise retailers carried RFID tags, and Apple sold an estimated 55 million AirTags in 2021-2022 on a crowd-sourced tracking network. Item-level tracking became routine inside the 2015-2025 band, so hit. Sterling's full vision (cradle-to-grave data for every object, recycling included) is not there yet; EU digital product passports start after 2025.

Within the 2015-2025 band, in-game item purchases became the main revenue of the games industry: all top-ten grossing digital games of 2019 were free-to-play, Fortnite cosmetics earned billions in 2018, and Newzoo put in-game purchases at about three-quarters of 2020 games revenue. Hundreds of millions of players owned virtual items, which meets the consumer test. Legal ownership stays platform-controlled and NFT-based ownership collapsed, but the label's ownership of virtual goods is mainstream.

A bare 'Sensors' label names a component class, not a product or practice. Sensors were already ubiquitous and networked in 2011 (smartphone GPS and accelerometers, industrial SCADA), so no adoption threshold separates before and after the 2015-2025 band. If read narrowly as IoT, connected devices reached about 18.8 billion in 2024 and it would be a hit, but the label does not fix that reading.

Test: medical standard practice (routine, reimbursed). Medicare telehealth visits rose 63-fold from about 840,000 in 2019 to 52.7 million in 2020, and about a third of behavioral health visits moved to telehealth. Reimbursement expanded in 2020, so it became routine practice inside the 2015-2025 band.

Medical test. By 2025 there were real approved products (36 gene therapies and 71 non-modified cell therapies worldwide), and FDA had granted 184 RMAT designations. But most are for rare diseases or cancers, with high prices and small patient numbers; pluripotent stem-cell products had dosed only about 1,200 patients in trials by end 2024. Tissue and organ regeneration is not routine practice. Real niche adoption at 2025 gives partial. Blood stem-cell transplants are routine but were routine long before 2011, so they do not make the forecast a hit.

Test: professional practice. HFT became the dominant source of US equity volume around 2008-2009 (Tabb estimates of 50-70% of volume by 2009-2010), and HFT revenues had already peaked in 2009. That puts mainstream status about 3 years before the placed year 2012. The early-forecast rule puts 3-5 years early in partial. Hit would need mainstream arrival within 2010-2014; the take-off came before that window.

Professional test. By 2012 AWS served hundreds of thousands of business and government customers in 190 countries, and S3 held 1.3 trillion objects. The 2013 RightScale survey found 75% of organizations already used cloud to some extent. Cloud was standard practice in IT at the placed year, so the distance is 0 years. Consumer cloud services (webmail, online storage) were also widespread by then.

Test: consumer feature shipped as standard on mass-market devices. Capacitive multi-touch became the default smartphone interface after the 2007 iPhone and Android, and Pew measured 46% of US adults owning a smartphone in early 2012. The 10% threshold was crossed around 2010, within 2 years of 2012, so the forecast was on time rather than late. Hit, not partial, because mainstream status and the placed year coincide.

Kinect brought consumer depth imaging to market in 2010 and reached 24 million units by February 2013, but it was an optional console peripheral, about one per three Xbox 360s, and Microsoft discontinued it in 2017. That is real but niche adoption against the consumer test (10%+ of households or a standard feature on mass-market devices). Depth sensing became a standard feature on mass-market devices with the iPhone X TrueDepth camera in late 2017, 5 years after 2012. Both routes give partial, not hit.

Consumer test. Pew measured 25% of US adults owning a tablet in August 2012 and 34% in May 2013. The threshold of roughly 10% was crossed in 2011-2012, which is inside the placed year. This is a hit, not early, because ownership was still below 10% when the iPad launched in 2010.

Test: consumer product (10%+ of people) or routine clinical practice. In 2012 physician-ordered and consumer whole-genome sequencing existed as a real but tiny commercial service; the $1,000 genome only arrived with Illumina HiSeq X in 2014. By 2019 Veritas, a leading consumer WGS provider, had sequenced about 5,000 genomes, while 26 million people had bought cheaper genotyping (not sequencing). It is not mainstream within 5 years of 2012, so this is partial only on the niche-adoption clause; it is close to a miss.

Industrial test. AM was real and routine for prototyping by 2012, but the whole industry was only $2.2 billion that year. By 2023 it reached about $20 billion, still a very small fraction of global manufacturing, and consumer 3D printers did not reach 10% of households. AM was real but niche at the placed year and is still not mainstream production practice 5+ years later. Partial for real niche adoption; not a hit because production use never became standard across manufacturing.

Quantitative test (D10: hit within 10%, partial within 25%). ITU counted 2.3 billion internet users at end-2011 and over 2.7 billion in 2013, so 2012 sits near 2.5 billion. The poster figure of 2 billion is about 20% low. That is inside 25% and outside 10%, so partial.

Quantitative test. Estimates for 2012 disagree because the definition of a connected device varies. Cisco put internet-connected devices at 8.7 billion in 2012; IDATE counted 15 billion connected machines and objects. Against Cisco the poster is about 15% high (partial); against IDATE it is 33% low (miss). Partial on the lower, internet-connected count, which matches the poster's wording.

Test: shipped as standard on mass-market devices. In 2013 Qi existed on a few phones (Nexus 4/5, some Lumias): real but niche. It became a standard flagship feature only with the Galaxy S8 and iPhone 8 in 2017, when about 500 million wireless-charging devices shipped. That is 4 years after 2013, so partial on both the niche and the distance criteria. Not a hit because 2013 adoption was far below mass-market level.

Quantitative test. The UN estimated world population at 7.2 billion in mid-2013. The poster figure of 7 billion is about 3% low, inside the 10% hit margin. The UN had marked the 7 billion day in October 2011, so the placement is slightly late but the number for 2013 is within tolerance.

Siri shipped in 2011, Google Now in 2012 and Cortana in April 2014, so by 2014 every major smartphone OS shipped a built-in assistant agent as a standard feature (consumer test, standard feature on mass-market devices). Pew found nearly half of US adults used a voice assistant by 2017. Mainstream status falls in 2012-2014, within 2 years of 2014. If the label means autonomous goal-directed agents, that arrived only around 2025 and would be a miss; I read the 2012 label as the assistant class.

Abstract-practice test. Stuxnet (2010) was a single early case. By 2014-2017 state cyber attacks were routine news: the FBI attributed the Sony Pictures attack to North Korea in December 2014, attacks hit the Ukrainian grid in 2015-2016, and NotPetya followed in 2017. Routine occurrence starts within 2 years of 2014, so this is a hit.

Test: consumer feature on mass-market devices. Kinect reached 24 million units by February 2013, close to the placed year 2014, but it was an add-on to one console line and never became a standard input on mass-market devices. Microsoft ended Kinect manufacturing in October 2017 and touchless gesture input did not replace it. Real adoption that then faded fits partial better than hit; it is not a miss because tens of millions of households used it around the placed year.

Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market devices). NFC shipped in 18% of 1.5 billion phones in 2013 and IHS expected 416 million NFC phones in 2014. Apple added NFC and Apple Pay to the iPhone 6 in September 2014, which made NFC standard on both major smartphone platforms. Mainstream falls at 2014 to 2016, within 2 years of the placed year.

Test: consumer feature shipped on mass-market devices. 3D-capable TVs reached about 20% of global flat-panel TV sales in 2013, but the feature sat on premium sets, actual usage stayed low, and Samsung, Sony, LG and others dropped 3D by 2016-2017. That is real but niche use around 2014 followed by abandonment, so partial under the lenient reading. Under the strict reading (true volumetric displays) the verdict is a clear miss: no volumetric display ever reached consumers.

In 2014 robot vacuums were a real niche: iRobot had sold about 10 million Roombas cumulatively by 2013, and iRobot's own filings still called global household penetration single digits in 2018. US household ownership now sits near 20-25%, so the 10% line in rich markets was crossed around 2019-2020, 5-6 years after 2014. Real but niche adoption by 2014 gives partial; the late crossing rules out hit.

Industrial/consumer test. As of 2024-2025, reviews and IDTechEx describe most self-healing technologies as developmental or early commercial, with niche use in coatings, some phone back covers and tires. They are not standard practice in any major field by 2019 (placed year + 5) or today. This is a miss, not a niche-based partial, because in 2014 the products were demonstrations and isolated items, not real adoption.

Test: consumer feature. Siri (2011) and Google voice search shipped speech recognition as a standard smartphone feature in the early 2010s, and in May 2017 Pew found 46% of US adults used voice assistants. Mass use arrived in the 2013-2017 range, within 2 years of the placed year 2015.

Abstract-practice test. By 2015, 68% of US adults owned a camera smartphone, and by 2016 47% of US general-purpose law enforcement agencies and 80% of large departments had body-worn cameras. Continuous video capture was routine and reported as normal around the placed year (distance 0 to 1 years). If the label is read narrowly as always-on wearable lifelogging cameras (Narrative Clip, Google Glass), the verdict would be miss, because that category failed.

Test: energy, material share of new capacity. Tidal stream was at demonstration scale in 2015; the largest array, MeyGen phase 1, is 6 MW (first power November 2016). Europe had about 32 MW cumulative tidal stream installed by 2024, a negligible share of capacity. Not mainstream within 5 years of 2015 or since. Demonstration plants do not qualify as niche adoption under the energy test, so miss, not partial.
Quantitative test. ITU counted 3.2 billion internet users in 2015. The poster figure of 2.5 billion is about 22% low: inside 25%, outside 10%, so partial. The poster underestimated internet growth.

Quantitative test. The Ericsson Mobility Report of November 2015 counted about 15 billion connected devices in 2015 (phones, PCs, tablets, consumer electronics, M2M and fixed phones). The poster figure matches within 10%, so hit. Ericsson counts mobile subscriptions as devices; a narrower count would be lower.

In 2016 Google switched Translate to neural machine translation and launched Google Assistant, while Alexa devices spread. Pew found 46% of US adults used voice assistants in 2017 and 25% owned a smart speaker by 2019. Natural language interfaces were a standard feature on mass-market phones and speakers in 2016-2018, within 2 years of 2016 (consumer test).

Infrastructure test. Ericsson counted 1 billion LTE subscriptions at end-2015 and reported LTE becoming the dominant global access technology in 2017-2018. In rich markets (US, Korea, Japan) LTE was already the majority by 2015-2016. Mainstream falls within 2 years of 2016, so this is a hit.

Test: standard feature on mass-market devices. Flexible AMOLED smartphone panel shipments rose from 40 million in 2016 to 125 million in 2017, driven by iPhone X and Samsung Galaxy flagships. Flexible panels became standard on flagship phones in 2016-2018, within 2 years of 2016. Foldable form factors stay niche, but the label is about flexible screens, which shipped at scale.

Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market vehicles). The EU made eCall, an embedded telematics unit, mandatory in all new car and van models from 31 March 2018. Counterpoint reported that over half of cars sold globally in 2020 were connected. Telematics became a standard feature between 2016 and 2020; the core shift lands within 2 years of 2016 (EU mandate 2018).

Test: medical, standard practice. As of 2025 reviews, no bioprinted solid organ has been transplanted as routine care; the field is in research and early clinical trials of simple tissues. Printed anatomical models for surgical planning exist but are not organ printing. Not mainstream within 5 years of 2016 (by 2021) or since, so miss.

In 2016 global fuel cell vehicle sales were in the low thousands (Mirai about 2,000 worldwide) and total fuel cell shipments were a few hundred megawatts, a rounding error against global power and vehicle markets. Shipments passed 1 GW only in 2019, still far from a material share of new capacity (energy test). Fuel cells stayed niche through 2021 and remain niche now; battery EVs took the vehicle role.

Industry test. Commercial cargo flights to the ISS (SpaceX Dragon) ran from 2012, so real but niche commercial activity existed by 2016. Commercial crew became routine only after Crew Dragon Demo-2 in May 2020, and private tourist flights (Blue Origin, Virgin Galactic, Inspiration4) started in 2021, 4-5 years after the placed year. Space tourism remains a few hundred people, so no reading makes this a hit; the niche 2016 activity and 2020 crew routine make it partial, not miss.

Test: consumer product at roughly 10%+ of households. Consumer mesh Wi-Fi launched in 2016 (eero, Google Wifi). Parks Associates found 11% of US broadband households had a mesh Wi-Fi product in 2019, and 32% of US internet households in 2025. The 10% threshold was crossed about 2019, 2 years after the placed year 2017, so it is a hit at the edge of the window.

Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market devices). Pokemon Go reached more than 500 million downloads in 2016. Apple shipped ARKit in iOS 11 in 2017 to hundreds of millions of iPhones and iPads, and Google followed with ARCore. Phone-based AR became a standard platform feature at the placed year (distance 0 to 1 years). Headset AR stayed niche, but the label does not require headsets.

Test: shipped as standard feature on mass-market devices. Fingerprint sensors reached 55-64% of global smartphone shipments in 2017 (TrendForce, Digitimes Research), and 21% of US adults regularly wore a smartwatch or fitness tracker with heart-rate sensing by 2019. Mainstream in 2016-2017, within 2 years of 2017. Hit.

Interactive whiteboards were already standard in UK classrooms before the poster: Futuresource put interactive display penetration at 87% by end 2012, 5 years before 2017, and interactive flat panels then replaced them. Outside education, interactive wall displays (Surface Hub, Jamboard) stayed niche in offices and absent from homes. Education reached mainstream about 5 years early and the wider ubicomp vision stayed niche, so partial, not hit.

Consumer test. Juniper estimated about $4.9bn smart toy revenue and 224 million units in 2017, a real market but a small share of a roughly $90bn global toy market, and much of it was toys-to-life figures that then collapsed. Flagship connected toys failed: Mattel discontinued Hello Barbie by 2017 and Germany banned My Friend Cayla in 2017. Real but niche adoption at the placed year gives partial; no evidence shows smart toys as mainstream by 2022.

Test: material share / standard use in mass products. Graphene reached real commercial niches (sports goods, coatings, battery and composite additives) by 2017, but the whole graphene market was only about $380 million in 2022 and peer-reviewed market analysis calls it mostly niche-scale. It is not mainstream within 5 years of 2017. It gets partial only on the niche-adoption clause, not miss, because products were on sale at the placed year.

Energy test. Advanced biofuels were real and commercial but small: about 9% of biofuels in 2018, while all renewables supplied only 3.7% of transport fuel. That is well below a material share of the fuel market at or 5 years after 2017. Partial for real niche adoption; not a miss because commercial advanced-biofuel volumes existed at the placed year. The label is vague; if it means conventional biofuels, those were already mainstream before 2012 and the call would be early-mainstream, not a forecast.

Test: infrastructure, widely deployed. In 2018 silicon photonics shipped in volume for the first time (about 1.3 million units, about USD 455 million, mainly Intel and Luxtera 100G transceivers in hyperscale data centers), a small share of the optical transceiver market. Real but niche adoption at the placed year, so partial. Broad deployment came later with 400G/800G AI data-center optics and co-packaged optics in the mid-2020s, 5+ years after 2018, which does not support a hit.

IHS Markit reported that 4K TVs were about 44% of global TV shipments in Q3 2018, and share passed half of shipments soon after. That is a standard feature on mass-market TVs in 2018, the placed year (consumer test).

Infrastructure test. EIA reports that nearly half of US electricity customers had smart meters in 2016 and that penetration passed 50% in every customer class in 2018 (56% overall). EU rollouts (Italy, Sweden, Spain) were largely complete by the late 2010s. Majority deployment arrives within 2 years of 2018, so this is a hit.

Test: consumer product at 10%+ share. Google cancelled Project Ara in September 2016 before launch, and Motorola Moto Mods and LG G5 modules faded. Surviving modular makers are small: Fairphone sold 22,623 phones in 2018 and about 95,000 in 2020. Real but tiny niche adoption existed at the placed year 2018, so this is partial on the niche clause; mainstream never happened, and it sits close to a miss.

Medical test. Robot-assisted prostatectomy was the majority US approach already by 2008 to 2013. Across general surgery in 73 Michigan hospitals, robotic use rose from 1.8% in 2012 to 15.1% in 2018, displacing laparoscopy. Robotic surgery was approved, reimbursed and routine across several specialties at the placed year (distance 0). Hit and not early-miss because broad multi-specialty routine use arrived around 2018, even though one procedure adopted it earlier.

Test: medical, approved and widely used. FDA has approved no hemoglobin-based oxygen carrier for human use; Hemopure is approved only in South Africa and Russia and is compassionate-use only in the US. No blood substitute is standard practice anywhere in major markets through 2026. Miss.

Desktop 3D printers had real niche adoption by 2018: Wohlers counted about 591,000 desktop units sold in 2018, mostly to hobbyists, schools and professionals. That is far below 10% of households in any rich market, and home fabrication has not become mainstream by 2023 or since. Real niche adoption by the placed year gives partial under D10; it was never mainstream.

Consumer test. Google Translate already had 200 million monthly users in April 2012 (about 9% of internet users) and over 500 million users by 2016, when neural MT shipped. Mainstream therefore arrived around 2013-2016, 3-6 years before the placed year: the forecast was late. I place the crossing at about 2014, 5 years early, which is partial; a stricter reading of the 2012 figure would make it a miss.

Test: consumer product at 10%+ of people. Pew found 16% of US adults had invested in, traded or used cryptocurrency by September 2021, and about 1 in 5 by 2026. The 10% line was crossed around 2020-2021, within 2 years of the placed year 2019.

Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market devices). Apple shipped the Taptic Engine in Apple Watch (2015), iPhone 6s (2015) and iPhone 7 (2016), with system-wide haptics in iOS. High-fidelity haptics then spread to flagship Android phones and game controllers. Mainstream arrived 2016 to 2019, within 3 years at most and most weight within 2 years of 2019. Plain vibration motors were mainstream long before 2012, so the reading of rich haptics is needed for the claim to be a forecast.

Test: medical, standard practice. CGM use in the T1D Exchange QI Collaborative rose from 59% (2016) to 72% (2021), and CGM became standard of care for type 1 diabetes around 2018-2020; home antigen tests also became routine in 2021. Mainstream in its field within 2 years of 2019. Hit. The label is broad: biomarkers as a lab concept predate 2012, and wearable sweat or multi-analyte biomarker sensing is still niche, so a stricter reading would give partial.

The embedded form failed: Samsung's Galaxy Beam projector phones sold poorly and no major phone maker ships a projector. Standalone portable mini projectors remain a real but small accessory category in 2019 and now. Real niche adoption by the placed year gives partial under D10. The ubicomp vision of projectors in everyday devices was abandoned, so this sits at the boundary with miss.

Consumer/infrastructure test. Waymo opened a paid robotaxi service in Phoenix in December 2018, with safety drivers and a small user group: real but niche adoption at the placed year. By 2024 (placed year + 5) Waymo gave about 100,000 rides per week in a few US cities, and about 500,000 per week in 2026, which is still far from mainstream. The niche-by-placed-year clause gives partial; mainstream adoption within 5 years did not happen.

Test: consumer use by 10%+ of people. Global Drug Survey data show 12-month use of stimulants or modafinil for performance rose from 4.9% (2015) to 13.7% (2017), but among a self-selected sample of drug users, not the general population. General-population use stays well below mainstream levels, but real niche use existed by 2019, so partial. If the smart-pill drug-delivery reading were meant instead, the result would be similar: approved but niche products.

Infrastructure test. Smart-grid components did become mainstream: 56% of US meters were advanced meters in 2018. But the segmented architecture itself stayed niche: the US installed a record 546 microgrids in 2019, a very small share of grid capacity. The distinctive part of the label had real but niche adoption at the placed year. Partial, not hit, because the grid was not re-architected into segments within 2 years of 2019.

Test: consumer service used by a large share of the population. No commercial sub-orbital passenger flight existed by 2019; Blue Origin started crewed flights in 2021 and Virgin Galactic in 2023. Blue Origin carried 98 people before pausing New Shepard for at least two years in January 2026; Virgin Galactic paused after June 2024 and targets 2027. A few hundred wealthy passengers is not mainstream, and there was no niche adoption by 2019. Miss.

In 2020 generated narrative was real but niche: AI Dungeon (GPT-2/GPT-3) had an enthusiast audience, and procedural narrative existed in some games. Mass use of generated stories came with ChatGPT and companion chatbots from 2023, 3 or more years after 2020, and story generation is still a minority use of those tools. Niche by the placed year gives partial; there is no evidence of mainstream use by 2020 for a hit.

Infrastructure test. 5G launched commercially in 2019. Ericsson reported about 35% 5G subscription penetration in North America and North East Asia by end-2022 and over 1 billion subscriptions globally; 5G phones were standard in mass-market lines from 2021. Mainstream in major markets by 2022 is within 2 years of 2020, so this is a hit.

Test: standard feature on mass-market devices. Face ID launched on iPhone X in 2017, and Counterpoint expected more than one billion smartphones with Face ID-style facial recognition shipped by 2020. Consumer machine vision became standard in 2017-2020, within 2 years of 2020. Industrial inspection vision was established earlier, but the consumer take-off matches the placed year.

Consumer test. In 2020 display glasses existed only as enterprise and developer products (Google Glass Enterprise, HoloLens 2, Vuzix, Epson). The first mass-brand consumer display glasses, Meta Ray-Ban Display at $799, launched only in September 2025. The 2025 smart-glasses boom (about 7 million units) was mostly display-less glasses. Real niche adoption at the placed year gives partial; display glasses were still far below 10% of people at the 5-year mark.

Test: medical/industrial standard practice. FDA cleared the ReWalk personal exoskeleton in 2014 and several medical and industrial models sell, so adoption by 2020 was real. It stays niche: high cost, low insurance coverage, and use limited to some rehab centers and pilot industrial sites through the mid-2020s. Real but niche adoption by the placed year, so partial, not hit.

By 2020 personalized medicines were 39% of FDA novel drug approvals, over a third for the third time in four years, and biomarker testing to select targeted therapy was standard of care in oncology (professional test). Adoption in primary care and pharmacogenomics stays thin, so the hit rests on oncology and drug development, where the practice was routine in the placed year.

Industrial/consumer test. By 2020 metamaterials had real niche products (for example metamaterial satellite antennas and radars). The first mass-market consumer part, the Metalenz metasurface in ST's time-of-flight sensor, shipped in 2022. Metamaterials are still a component in a few product lines, not a standard feature across mass-market devices, so this is partial (niche by placed year), not hit.

Test: energy, a material share of new PV capacity. BIPV stays under 1% of installed PV capacity worldwide (Switzerland near 10% is the exception). Commercial PV glass products existed by 2020, so this is real niche adoption and partial, not miss. It is not mainstream within 5 years of 2020.

Consumer test. No tourist flew in 2020, and no commercial service operated that year. Blue Origin, Virgin Galactic and SpaceX private missions started in 2021 to 2023, but total flyers stayed in the low hundreds and seats cost from hundreds of thousands to tens of millions of dollars. It was not mainstream within 5 years (by 2025) and remains a luxury niche. Miss rather than partial because no commercial space tourism operated at the placed year; the pre-2009 Soyuz tourist flights had stopped.

Quantitative test. ITU counted 4.1 billion users in 2019 and 10.2% growth in 2020, which gives about 4.5 billion in 2020, and 4.9 billion in 2021. The 2020 figure sits inside the poster's 4-5 billion range, so hit.

Quantitative test. IoT Analytics counted 21.7 billion active connected devices at end-2020 (11.7 billion IoT and about 10 billion non-IoT). The low end of the poster range, 30 billion, is about 38% above the actual figure, beyond the 25% partial margin, so miss. The poster copied the 2011-era industry forecasts (Cisco, Ericsson) that all overshot.

Quantitative test. In 2020 the best consumer prices were about $14 per TB (a 14 TB WD Elements near $190), so $150 bought about 10 TB. Backblaze paid $0.014 per GB even in late 2022, which is about 11 TB for $150. The poster figure is about 20 times too high, so miss.

Quantitative test. Consumer PCs in 2020 shipped with 8-16 GB of RAM, and in 2026 the Steam Hardware Survey still shows 16 GB as the most common configuration (about 41%). The poster figure is about 50 times too high, so miss.

Test: consumer or professional interface in wide use. By 2021 products marketed as holographic existed (Looking Glass light-field displays from USD 349, Microsoft HoloLens 2 with diffractive waveguides), but sales were small and mostly professional. True electro-holographic displays remain lab technology. Real but niche adoption at the placed year gives partial; if only true holography counts, the verdict is miss.

The forecast was late. Google Now shipped context-aware cards (location, time, calendar, traffic) in Android 4.1 in 2012, Apple added proactive suggestions in iOS 9 in 2015, and location triggers and sensor adaptation were standard on mass-market phones by then (consumer test). Mainstream by about 2012-2015 is 6-9 years before 2021, beyond the 5-year limit, so miss under the early-forecast rule.

Any test. Visible-light cloaks remain laboratory demonstrations limited to small objects, narrow angles or specific polarizations. No commercial or military product exists in 2026, the end of the 5-year window. There is no niche adoption either, so this is a clear miss.

Test: energy, a material share of capacity. Piezoelectric floors and pavements remain demonstrations: a Tokyo station floor with 400,000 daily walkers powers only some LEDs, and reviews cite low power density and high cost. Uses stay at self-powered sensors and show installations, not energy supply. Demonstrations do not count as niche adoption under the energy test, so miss.

Abstract-practice test. Cloud seeding runs operationally in more than 50 countries, and in December 2020 China announced a plan to cover 5.5 million square km with artificial rain or snow by 2025. But these programs are regional, their efficacy is still scientifically contested, and weather engineering is not a normal tool for most governments or water users. Real but niche adoption at the placed year gives partial. Not a hit because operational seeding predates 2012 by decades and did not become a general practice; not a miss because state-scale programs exist and grew around 2021.

The label gives no testable threshold. Platform ratings (eBay, Amazon, Uber, Airbnb) already existed in 2012 and were mainstream by about 2015; under that reading the forecast was 7+ years late, a miss. Under the stronger reading of a cross-platform reputation currency (Klout-style scores), the concept failed: Klout shut down in 2018. The two readings give opposite outcomes and neither is clearly what the label means, so the claim is too vague to grade.

After the FAA Part 107 rule in 2016, commercial drone use became routine in surveying, inspection, agriculture and media. The FAA counted about 255,000 certificated remote pilots at end 2021 and about 380,000 registered non-recreational drones in 2022. That meets the professional test (standard practice in its fields) by 2020-2022, within 2 years of 2022. Delivery drones remain niche but are not required for the label.

Consumer test. Singapore approved cultivated chicken in December 2020 and the USDA approved Upside Foods and Good Meat in June 2023, with sales limited to a few restaurants. This is real but niche adoption around the placed year, so partial. It is far from 10% of consumers, and several US states have since banned it; if the niche clause is set aside, it heads toward a miss by 2027.

Test: standard feature on mass-market devices. Google HDR+ (2014), portrait modes (2016), Apple Smart HDR (2018) and Google Night Sight (2018) made computational photography the default pipeline on mass-market smartphones by 2018-2019. That is 4-5 years before the placed year 2023. The forecast was late, and the early rule puts 3-5 years early in partial.

Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2028. Consumer test. The first large-area display textile appeared as a lab result in Nature in 2021, and a 2024 review still frames integrated textile displays as a research goal. No fabric display product is sold at scale; LED-studded fashion garments are not screens and remain boutique items. Nothing approaches mainstream at the placed year. The 5-year window closes in 2028; given lab status in 2024 the miss is very likely to stand.

Test: industrial standard practice. CNTs became a standard conductive additive in lithium-ion electrodes for EV batteries, with demand growing from about 3,000 t (2019) toward 13,000 t (2024) and large capacity expansions at LG Chem, Cnano and others. That puts mainstream industrial use around 2021-2024, within 2 years of 2023. Hit under this reading; if the poster meant structural CNT materials or CNT electronics, those remain niche and the verdict would be partial.

If telepresence means everyday video presence, it became mainstream in 2020 when Zoom reached 300 million daily meeting participants, 4 years before 2024, which is partial. If it means immersive or robotic telepresence (Google Beam/Starline, Vision Pro personas, telepresence robots), it had real but niche adoption in 2024, which is also partial. Neither reading gives mainstream within 2 years of 2024.

The label names a research discipline, not a product or practice with an adoption threshold. Its boundary with ordinary genetic and metabolic engineering is contested even among experts, so recombinant insulin (1982), mRNA vaccines (2020) or nothing at all could each be claimed as the mainstream moment. No measurement can confirm or refute 'synthetic biology becomes mainstream around 2024'.

Quantitative test. In 2024 mainstream laptops shipped with 512 GB to 1 TB SSDs, and the largest hard drive of any kind, Seagate's 30 TB Mozaic 3+, went only to hyperscale data centres. Standard storage was about 1,000 times below 1 PB, so miss.

The label does not say what counts as a 'lifeform' (scripted NPC, LLM agent, artificial-life simulation) or what 'mainstream' would mean for one. Under a loose reading it was already true decades ago (artificial-life simulations, game NPCs); under a strict reading (autonomous, self-replicating digital organisms) there is no test. LLM-driven agent societies such as Stanford's Generative Agents (2023) exist, but no adoption metric separates success from failure.

Quantitative test, threshold claim. The $999 Nvidia RTX 5080 (2025) does 56 TFLOPS at FP32 and 225 TFLOPS at dense FP16, which is 18 and 4.4 times short of 10^15. Only NVIDIA's low-precision sparse 'AI TOPS' figure (about 1,800 TOPS) passes the threshold. The number is met only under the loosest reading of 'calculation', so partial, not hit. The brain-equivalence part of the label is not testable and is not graded.

Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2031. Infrastructure test. NASA runs DTN operationally only in Earth orbit (ISS payloads, since 2009) and plans it for the Moon via LunaNet, whose interoperability specification was published in February 2025. The Mars Relay Network uses 4 orbiters to relay data for 2 landed assets, but DTN on deep-space links is still at analysis and demonstration stage. No interplanetary internet exists in 2026. The window closes in 2031.

Test: shipped as standard on mass-market devices. Microsoft put FPGAs in nearly every Azure server from 2015, so reconfigurable computing is standard in part of hyperscale infrastructure, about 10 years before the placed year. In consumer devices, FPGAs appear only as hidden glue logic in some phones; users and developers do not reprogram them, and mainstream consumer compute uses fixed-function NPUs and GPUs. Real but niche adoption at the placed year, so partial. The window closes 2031.

Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2031. As of mid-2026 no general-purpose home robot has reached households at scale. 1X opened NEO pre-orders at $20,000 in late 2025 with first deliveries promised for 2026, and reports up to July 2026 found no verified customer delivery. That is not even niche adoption yet, so neither hit nor niche partial applies now. The window closes in 2031.

Medical test. The FDA approved the first mesenchymal stromal cell therapy (Ryoncil) in December 2024 for a narrow paediatric indication. Japan gave conditional, time-limited approval to the first two iPSC-derived products (Parkinson's and heart failure) in March 2026, tested in 6-8 patients. This is real but niche adoption at the placed year, so partial. Hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation has been standard since before 2012; if the label includes it, the forecast was more than 5 years late and a miss.

Test: material share of the market. Bioplastics are about 0.5% of the roughly 414 million tonnes of plastic produced each year, and the share is flat because fossil plastic grows too. Bio-based materials are a real commercial niche at the placed year 2026, so partial on the niche clause. If the label meant medical biomaterials, it would be a late forecast and a miss.

Energy test. Niche products exist and are real: EnOcean kinetic self-powered switches (several million installed, in over a million buildings) and kinetic watches. Wearable body-motion harvesters (piezoelectric, triboelectric, knee generators) remain mostly research or small specialist products, and they supply no material share of device power. Real niche adoption at the placed year gives partial. It is not mainstream, and reviews still list commercialization barriers.

Test: industrial standard practice or material market share. Vertical farms exist and sell leafy greens, so adoption is real, but they supply a tiny share of produce. The sector contracted: AeroFarms went bankrupt in 2023, Bowery shut in 2024, Plenty filed Chapter 11 in 2025, and 14 indoor-farm bankruptcies occurred in 2025. Real but niche at the placed year, so partial; not a miss because the practice is not abandoned.
